words.description: Durably pause all activity (agent turns, timers that would wake an agent). Like resume, only the owner from a channel on this machine: `by` cites the one owner message that said stop.
Resume after a pause. Only the owner can, from a channel on this machine, after an explicit confirmation.
Read the hub's settings (all of them, or the named keys). Credentials are never part of the result.
Change settings: the body is the keys to change and their new values. Agents asking for this are asked about by the owner.
Choose the main model (provider and model name) the hub's own agents run on; restart_required says whether an agent must be restarted for it to apply.
List the plugins of the agent runtime and whether each is enabled.
Enable or disable a plugin of the agent runtime. Plugins change what an agent can do, so an agent asking for this is asked about by the owner.
The hub's state in a few facts: the time and time zone, whether activity is paused, the version, how long it has been up, how many agents and hands are online.
The hub's recent log lines (default 200, newest last). Only the owner, from a channel on this machine: logs can hold things nobody else should see.
A setting was changed (the key names, never the values). Goes into the ledger so that what changed, when and by whom can be found again.
Inspect the current approval rules (who may use which capability without asking, until when) and the approval mode. Do not assume a risky action is already allowed.

Allow one agent to use one outside capability without asking, for up to 30 days, optionally only for one target (site:<host>, a calendar id, a recipient id, browse). The owner is always asked when an agent requests it.
Remove a known approval rule. It changes future decisions, not past actions. The owner is always asked when an agent requests it.
Switch the approval mode: auto asks only when an outside action needs it; always asks about every outside action that is not a read. The owner is always asked when an agent requests it.
Approval evidence, newest first: what was asked, the facts the reviewer saw and its verdict, the card shown, the owner's answer, and whether the action then ran.
Review earlier gate decisions (who asked for what and how it was decided). Read only.
The requests you made that are waiting for the owner or have been answered and not yet acted on. Only the agent that made a request sees it.
One pending request of yours: the original request, its state and the owner's answer. Use it before redeeming, to be sure the action is still wanted.
Carry out a request the owner approved: the original request is sent again and, this time, passes the gate as approved. Works once, only for the agent that made it, in its own turn.
Say that you will not carry out a request that was answered, for example because it is no longer wanted. The owner is told.
Withdraw a question or approval request you made, while it is still waiting; the owner's card is taken down.
Which credentials are saved (names and kinds only, never a value).
Whether one credential is saved, and what it is for. A value is never returned.
Save a credential in the vault. Only the owner, from a channel on this machine; the value is held sealed and never reaches the ledger or an agent.
Delete a saved credential. Only the owner, from a channel on this machine.
A credential was saved or removed. Names only; the value is never on the ledger. The agents module listens to configure the runtime's own credentials.
Every hand the hub knows: name, kind, whether online, what the owner allowed it (lend capabilities, serve as a body, run local agents, web chat) and its tier.
One hand in detail: how it connects, what it was allowed, when it was last seen.
Start pairing a new computer or browser. The pairing code is shown only to the owner; you get a pair_id and, as the pairing moves on, a background message. Use pair_status to look.
Where a pairing is: waiting for the code, requested (the owner is asked), approved, connected, rejected or expired.
The pairing requests that are waiting for the owner's decision.
Approve a pairing request, with what the new hand may do: lend capabilities, serve as a body, run local agents, web chat; and its tier. An agent asking for this is always asked about by the owner.
Reject a pairing request.
Disconnect a hand and revoke it: it can no longer connect, and its capabilities and body go away. An agent asking for this is always asked about by the owner.
Let a revoked hand pair again, with the permissions it had. Only the owner.
Change the name a hand is shown with.
Change what a hand may do (lend capabilities, serve as a body, run local agents, web chat) and its tier (ask, full). An agent asking for this is always asked about by the owner.

Have a computer update its Ash program to the given version (checked against sha256). Approved here once; the update itself is then run by the hub. An agent asking for this is always asked about by the owner.
Show the pairing code of a pairing the owner started, with the address to open on the new computer. Only the owner, from a channel on this machine.
A pairing moved on (requested, approved, rejected, connected, expired). The one who started it is told by a background message.
A hand reports that one of its own permissions or switches changed (config.*). Sent by the hands module; not recorded.
Every live connection: which hand, which channels are open (device, human, agent), local or through the relay, since when, heartbeat delay.
One connection in detail: each channel's state, calls in flight, the latest disconnect and its reason code. Give hand or conn.
A health check: is the relay reachable, the state of each tunnel, the latest handshake failures with what their codes mean, clock difference, whether a capability list was refused.
Close one connection. The hand may reconnect by itself unless it was revoked.
Ask the relay to open the tunnel again, or tell a local hand to reconnect.
Ask a hand to send its capability list again, for example after you changed what it may lend.
The relay: whether there is one, its address, whether it is claimed by this hub, whether the hub is connected to it, the latest error.
Start building a relay in the owner's Cloudflare account: a 'sign in to Cloudflare' card goes to the owner. You get a setup_id and a background message at each step.
Where a relay setup is: waiting_login, authorized, deploying, claimed, connected, or failed with the reason.
Deploy the relay in the owner's account, claim it and connect. An agent asking for this is asked about by the owner.
Cancel a relay setup that is not finished.
Use an existing relay at this address instead of building one. An agent asking for this is asked about by the owner.
A hand finished the handshake and is connected. Goes into the ledger.
A hand's connection closed, with the close code and reason. Goes into the ledger.
A connection attempt failed the handshake (4001 identity, 4003 revoked, 4008 version, ...). Not recorded; service:link/diagnose reports the recent ones.

The host reports that the network or the power state changed (what: network with the proxy and whether the device is online, or power with whether it is in power-saving mode); the link layer reconnects the relay. Sent by the host module; not recorded.
Every declared agent: id, name, what it does, whether it is idle, working or stopped, and which one is primary.
The agent runtimes available (in the main body, and on computers allowed to host agents) with their models. Query before declaring an agent that runs on a computer.
The delegated work in flight (threads between agents).
Stop one delegated thread of work.
One agent's declaration (role, tools, lanes, modules, where it lives) and its state.
Put a question to another agent; the answer it gives in the turn that takes the question is the result.
Deliver news to another agent; what it says back is passed to the sender later as a message.
An agent's words in a turn that answers a question or news delivered to it. Only the agent that was asked, in that turn.

Declare a new agent: who it is, its role (brief), its tools and word policy, its lanes, which prompt modules it loads, and where it runs (native). It starts at once in its own session. Delegation rule: when the caller is not the owner, the tools and words you give the agent must be a subset of the tools and words you have yourself; anything beyond that is refused with forbidden. This is not a question to the owner. Delegation goes at most three levels deep.

Change an agent's declaration; it applies from its next turn. `primary` can be handed to another agent only through primary.set. Delegation rule: when the caller is not the owner, the tools and words you give the agent must be a subset of the tools and words you have yourself; anything beyond that is refused with forbidden. This is not a question to the owner. Delegation goes at most three levels deep.
Let a stopped agent take turns again.
Stop an agent: its current turn is cancelled and it leaves the registry, so words sent to it answer offline until it starts again. Only the owner can stop the primary agent.
Cancel an agent's current turn and restart its process; its sessions are resumed.
Remove a declared agent. The primary agent cannot be removed; hand `primary` to another one first.
Make another agent the primary one: the owner's words, the notification and island replies, and the semantic layer's wake-ups go to it. Only the owner.

Run one task on a temporary agent: declare it, hand it the task, collect the result and delete it, in one step. A quick result is returned, a slow one as a receipt. It can never do more than you can. Delegation rule: when the caller is not the owner, the tools and words you give the agent must be a subset of the tools and words you have yourself; anything beyond that is refused with forbidden. This is not a question to the owner. Delegation goes at most three levels deep.
Which resumable session an agent holds for a lane (the opaque handle the driver gave), or null.
Point a lane of an agent at a given session handle so the next turn resumes it; with no handle the lane starts fresh.
Open a new session for a lane of an agent. The old one is kept in the agent's own history; the ledger still has everything that was said.
Open a new session with the current static prompt modules (persona, rules). Done only when the agent is idle; skipped if nothing changed.
Compact the context of a lane's session, when the agent is idle. If it is busy the answer is conflict and the hub tries again after the turn.
Send messages to an idle agent and open a turn on a lane.
Queue messages for the agent's next turn on a lane, without interrupting the one running.
Say something into the turn that is running on a lane, so the agent takes it into account now.
Put content into a lane's session without starting a turn: named prompt modules, or plain text.
Stop the turn that is running on a lane.
Restart the agent's process and resume its sessions (one lane, or all when key is left out).

Set the runtime's own configuration for an agent (model, effort level, other options the runtime reports it supports), or read it when config is left out. The runtime keeps the truth; the hub stores no copy.
List, enable or disable the plugins of one agent's runtime. Plugins change what the agent can do, so an agent asking for this is asked about by the owner.

The host reports that the network or the power state changed (what: network with the proxy and whether the device is online, or power with whether it is in power-saving mode); the agents module restarts what needs it. Sent by the host module; not recorded.
An agent driver's model usage, passed to service:cost.
Every app found in the container (/root/apps/<id>/app.json): name, version, whether the owner installed (granted) it and whether it is running.
One app: what it needs from ash (needs), its screens (surfaces), events and tools.

Install an app from /root/apps/<id>/ (ash's own, or one you wrote): it is checked first as apps.validate does, and a failing app is refused with the problems (error.detail.problems) before anyone is asked. Then the owner approves, on one card, everything it needs (needs); an app you wrote is shown as written by you, not published. Then its grants are stored and it starts as member app:<id>. Installing again after editing restarts it with the new files.
Start an installed app that was turned off, within the grants the owner already gave. An agent's request asks the owner.
Stop an app; its grants are kept so it can be turned on again.
Take back one need (need: a member id such as device:<hand_id>, or notify / widgets / card), or every grant when need is left out, which stops the app.
Read /root/apps again: new apps appear, removed ones stop.

Restart an installed app's server so edits to its files (server.mjs, tools, app.json cards) take effect. It is checked first as apps.validate does: a failing app is not restarted and the problems come back (error.detail.problems). If app.json's needs changed, use apps.install instead (the owner approves them). Pages need no restart.

An app's recent output: what its server wrote to stderr, protocol errors (anything but MCP on stdout), and Ash's notes on starts, exits and restarts (newest last, default 100 lines, at most 400). last_exit says how the server last ended (exit code or signal); error is why it is not running, if Ash knows.

Empty the app's data folder (app.json data_dir, e.g. /root/apps/<id>/data) and restart it, so it starts over with no data; its cards redraw. Only for an app that declares data_dir. The owner's data is gone afterwards: do it only when the owner wants it, or for an app you are still building.

Uninstall an app: stop it, drop everything the owner granted it and its home-screen cards, and delete its folder /root/apps/<id>/. keep_data: true keeps the folder (its data and files) so it can be installed again as it was. Ash's own apps cannot be removed (they come back): disable them instead.

The ash-app/1 contract for writing an app, in full (doc, markdown): app.json fields, how ash starts the server and talks to it, pages (ui:// resources), tools, needs, events, listens. Also the app.json JSON Schema and a small runnable example app (hello: a list with one page and four tools, the same skeleton apps.scaffold writes) with its files. The same doc and example are in the container at doc_path and example.path.

Write a new app's skeleton into /root/apps/<id>/ (app.json, a dependency-free server.mjs, one ui/<page>.html per surface, shared ui/app.css and ui/app.js, an empty data/ folder). It runs as it is: a small working list in data/data.json with tools <id>.list, <id>.add, <id>.done (mark done/undone), <id>.remove, and a first page with the list and done/undone toggles. Change them to what the app is about; tools you name besides those answer with a placeholder until you write them in server.mjs. role (default: summary) says what the app is for and when to use it; you and Ash see it in every conversation. surfaces default to one page home: give the app tools that read and change its data, so you can do through them everything the owner does on its pages. Refuses a folder that already has an app.json. No approval is needed: it only writes files. Then edit, apps.validate, and apps.install (the owner approves what it needs).

Check an app folder the way install will: app.json against the contract (each missing or wrong field by its path), the icon file, then a trial start of its server (it must start and speak MCP over stdio), its tools (names, input schemas) and every page (each surface's ui:// resource must be served as HTML). Give id (the folder /root/apps/<id>) or path (/root/apps/<folder>). ok is true when nothing would stop it from installing and opening; warnings are worth fixing but do not block. Nothing is installed or changed.

The page resource of one of an app's surfaces (the ui:// resource its app.json lists), for a channel to show; csp lists the domains the page declared it may connect to and load from. Pages talk to the app through the bridge, not through this word.
The icon file of an app (base64 in data), for a channel to show in its list of apps.

Set a timer that sends a word to a member at a time (at, Unix ms) or repeatedly (every, seconds, at least 60). Use for a future or repeating message, not for immediate delivery. Keep the returned id to cancel it.
Cancel a timer by id; check `cancelled` because it may already have fired.
The active timers, to look at before changing them; the result is a snapshot.
The host's alarm went off (the device woke); the clock checks which timers are due. Sent by the host module.

A short completion from the hub's small model (the model argument is optional). For organs that must judge something in code, e.g. a sensor rule. The usage is counted against the caller and its quota.
One call of the hub's small model (the approval review, JEV, the progress summary, service:llm/complete), passed to service:cost under the caller's name.
The approved versions of SOUL.md and IDENTITY.md, the only ones sessions load. Editing the files in the body changes nothing until a change is proposed and approved.
Propose a new SOUL.md or IDENTITY.md with the reason. The owner is always asked when an agent proposes; a change the owner makes takes effect at once. It shows in new sessions after the next reload.

What is on the owner's phone home screen: each placed widget (the 'ash' widget, or an 'Ash 卡片' card widget with the card it shows), and every card that exists with its owner, size, expiry, event action names and the phone's last problem drawing it (null when it drew fine or has not reported).

Create or replace (same id) a card the owner can place on the phone home screen with the 'Ash 卡片' widget; widgets already showing it redraw. When the data belongs to an app (a todo list, health numbers…), use that app's own card instead (owner app:<id> in widget.list, drawn from the app's data and kept current; the owner places it on the home screen) — a copy of its data here goes stale. id: lowercase letters, digits, . _ - (at most 64); title: at most 40 characters. The card belongs to whoever created it: only its creator or the owner may replace or remove it. size is the intended widget size (2x2 small, 4x2 wide, 4x4 large). ttl_min: after this many minutes the card shows as expired until updated. Invalid cards are refused with the component, property and reason. The result says whether the phone drew it (phone: drawn), could not (phone: problem, with problem), or did not answer in time (unknown); a later problem (e.g. an image that failed to load) reaches you as widget.problem. When the phone can draw it, the result also carries a preview image of the card as the home screen shows it (at the widget's size, in the phone's current dark or light theme): look at it, and fix cut-off text, overflow and empty lists before telling the owner it is done. widget.card.preview shows it again later. a2ui is A2UI v0.9 (basic catalog) as a flat component list: {components:[{id, component, ...}], root?:'root', data?:{...}, sizes?, theme?:{primaryColor}}. Anything Android widgets can draw is allowed; what they cannot is refused with the reason. No limit on nesting style, number of buttons or text lines except Android's own (about 10 nested levels; a scrolling List's items get their own budget). Components: Text {text, variant: h1..h5|body|caption} — text keeps line breaks and emoji, and simple Markdown (**bold**, *italic*, `code`, ~~strike~~, [link](url), # heading, - list) is drawn as formatting, never shown raw. Row/Column {children, justify: start|center|end|spaceBetween|spaceAround|spaceEvenly|stretch, align: start|center|end|stretch}; Stack {children, align} (children overlap; a child's style.place: topStart..bottomEnd); Grid {children, columns}; Card {child}; List {children, columns?} scrolls vertically when longer than the widget (horizontal lists are impossible; at most 16 Lists per layout); Tabs {tabs:[{title, child}], selected?} (switches on the phone); Spacer {size?} (flexible when no size); Divider {axis}; Image {url, fit: contain|cover|fill|none|scaleDown, variant: icon|avatar|smallFeature|mediumFeature|largeFeature|header} with url https://… or data:image/png|jpeg|webp|gif;base64,… (the phone fetches, downsizes and caches; no SVG), 'avatar' / 'avatar:<face>' (Ash), 'icon:<name>'; Icon {name: an A2UI icon name (check, close, star, favorite, home, settings, refresh, add, delete, edit, mail, phone, person, search, share, warning, info, …) or Ash's sun, cloud, rain, snow, wind, moon, heart, steps, weight, sleep, water, fire, calendar, clock, alert, bell, car, money, chart; or {svgPath}}; Button {child: any component id, variant: default|primary|borderless, action}; CheckBox / Switch {label, value: bool or {path}}; ChoicePicker {options:[{label, value}], value:[...] or {path}, variant: mutuallyExclusive|multipleSelection, displayStyle: checkbox|chips}; ProgressBar {value, max?: 100, label?}; Badge {text}; Clock {format?, timeZone?} (live); Timer {since | until: epoch ms} (live count up/down). Not drawable in a widget (refused): Video, AudioPlayer, TextField, DateTimeInput, Slider, Modal, web pages, scripts, animation. Every component may have: weight (share of the free space in a Row/Column), visible (bool or {path}), accessibility {label}, action, and style {background, color (text/icon/tint; inherited by children), cornerRadius, padding, margin, width, height (dp | 'fill' | 'wrap'), fontSize (sp), fontWeight (normal|medium|bold|100-900), italic, underline, strikethrough, textAlign, maxLines, ellipsize (end|start|middle|none), lineHeight, letterSpacing, opacity}. Colours: '#RRGGBB', '#RRGGBBAA' (alpha last, e.g. '#000000B3' translucent dark), theme names text, textSecondary, accent, onAccent, background, surface, surfaceVariant, line, transparent, translucentDark, translucentLight, white, black, red, orange, yellow, green, teal, blue, purple, pink, gray (these follow the phone's dark mode), or {light, dark}. A background on the root replaces the widget's own background (and its title). Actions (any element; in a List each item is tappable): {event:{name, context?}} — sent back to you as widget.action with the item key, checked state or chosen values; {openApp:{app, surface?}} or {functionCall:{call:'openUrl', args:{url:'ui://<app>/<surface>'}}} — opens that app's page in 「Ash 应用」; {openAsh:{}}; openUrl with https/mailto/tel/geo. A CheckBox/Switch/ChoicePicker whose value is {path} writes the owner's choice back into the card's data. Values may be literals, {path:'/a/b'} into data (relative paths inside templates), or A2UI functions {call: formatString ('${/a} ${b}') | formatNumber | formatCurrency | formatDate | pluralize | and | or | not, args}. children may be a template {componentId, path:'/items'}: one copy per array element, with paths relative to the element (its id or key field is the item key in widget.action). sizes: [{width, height (dp), root}] gives other layouts for other widget sizes. Example: {components:[{id:'root',component:'Column',style:{background:'translucentDark',color:'white',padding:14},children:['t','l']},{id:'t',component:'Text',text:'**待办**',variant:'h3'},{id:'l',component:'List',children:{componentId:'row',path:'/todo'}},{id:'row',component:'CheckBox',label:{path:'title'},value:{path:'done'},action:{event:{name:'toggle'}}}],data:{todo:[{id:'a',title:'买菜',done:false}]}}

Look at a card again: the phone draws it as the home-screen widget would (its size on this phone, in the current dark or light theme) and returns the picture as an image you can see, or says why it cannot. Use it after the owner changes theme, after an app's card refreshed, or to check a card you did not just put. fresh: false means the phone did not answer in time and the image is the last one it drew.

Read one card back: what it says (its a2ui as it was put), size, owner, last update, the owner's answers recorded on it (feedback: what a feedback button said and when; card_updated_at tells which version of the card was answered), and the picture of how the home screen shows it now (the same image as widget.card.preview; preview_problem says why there is none). Use it to see what you showed before and how it was received; widget.list only gives titles.

Check a card's a2ui exactly as widget.card.put would, without saving or showing anything: valid, or the problem (which component, which property, why). levels is how deep it nests against Android's limit. Same format as widget.card.put.
Remove a card you created (the owner may remove any). Widgets that showed it ask the owner to pick another card.
The owner tapped, toggled or chose something on a card (sent from the phone as the owner). Owner only; the card's creator is then told by widget.action.

label.doing: 在转达小组件上的点击

words.description: The phone reports which Ash widgets are on its home screen. Sent by the hands module from the hand's event; not recorded.
The owner picked which card one placed 'Ash 卡片' widget shows. Sent by the hands module from the hand's event; not recorded.

label.doing: 在记下小组件选的卡片

words.description: What a channel reports after being asked to show widget state: which widgets are placed and which cards it drew, with the problem or a preview picture. Turned from the channel's present result by the human module; not recorded.

label.doing: 在记下卡片画出来没有

words.description: The owner tapped, toggled or chose something on a home-screen card. owner is the card's creator, who decides what it means; component is the element, item the list item's key, checked / value the new state. On an app's card (owner app:<id>) the tap goes to the app's own action tool, which changes the app's data; otherwise the tap itself does nothing else.

label.doing: 在转达小组件上的点击

words.description: The home-screen cards changed: the whole state for the channels that show widgets (the human edge pushes it as present{widget}). A channel that just connected gets the current state from service:widgets/widget.list.
The phone could not fully draw a home-screen card (problem says what and why); the card's creator should fix it.

Your pulse: whether it is active (it exists only while an 'Ash 卡片' widget is on the home screen; otherwise active:false, reason:'no widget'), whether the owner has it switched on, your wake schedule, today's wake count against the daily budget, the next scheduled wakes, the latest history entries and gaps you noted.

Change your own pulse and say why (reason is required and is kept in the history). Schedule (list of {time:'HH:MM' local, days:'daily'|'weekdays'|'weekends'|[0..6 with 0 = Sunday]} or {time:{at: epoch ms}} for one moment; replaces the whole list; the next 48 hours become real timers). Other fields are refused. PULSE.md, the file that tells you how to use each wake, is in your home folder: edit it there yourself.

Page through your pulse history, newest first: wakes (why, when), what you did (pulse.note), the owner's feedback on your cards, changes to the schedule with their reasons, skipped wakes and why. limit (default 20), before: an entry id from next_before to read older ones.

Record what you did on this wake and why (did, why, data_used: what you looked at). kind: pulse (default) for an ordinary wake, gap for something you wanted to know or do but could not get; gaps are collected so the missing source can be added. Nothing here ever reaches the owner.
Wake yourself now as a pulse to try your schedule and cards; it does not use the daily budget. Needs the pulse to be active and switched on.
Owner only: switch the whole pulse on or off. Off keeps PULSE.md, history and feedback.

Internal: the clock reports one of the semantic layer's own timers: wake (an hourly pulse), daily (the evening look back at the day) or reload (the daily new session). The hub itself calls this; nobody else.

label.doing: 在响应到点的主动更新

words.description: What the models used and cost: today, 7 and 30 days, by part of Ash, by day, and the latest calls.
The provider account balance for the configured API key; fails rather than reporting zero when it cannot be read.
Whether an agent may open another turn under its daily quota, by the latest usage numbers. A soft limit: the numbers are only as fresh as the last poll.

One model call, as the llm edge reports it for the hub's small models or an agent driver reports it for an agent: who called, which model, tokens in and out, the cost in US dollars when a price is known (the field is left out otherwise, never zero), whether it worked. Not recorded: usage has its own table.

The owner spoke while an agent was busy: judge what to do with it (stop it, pause, say it into the running turn, or wait for the next turn). Keywords first, the small model when unclear; a failed judgment means followup.
After a turn ended normally, label how it ended from the owner's point of view, for the island and the capsule: delivered, needs a reply, needs action in Ash, or incomplete.
Stop only the task the owner selected, never a newer turn.
End the selected capsule interaction: stop its current turn and withdraw only the pending requests that are displayed. Never stops a newer turn.

Before a turn that the owner started opens: decide whether the turn's phone-screen work belongs on the real screen or on a background virtual screen, and give the text to put into that turn. The agent names the lane because the turn does not have an id yet. Whatever cannot be judged (no phone, no judge, unsure) is mode none with no text: the turn goes on untouched.

label.doing: 在判断在哪块屏幕上做

words.description: After a turn ended: close the virtual screen this turn opened when its work is done, if the screen state the decision saw is still current. The real screen is never touched; the owner chooses when to go back to Ash.
Archived sensor readings of one kind in a time range (Unix ms; default the last day), oldest first. Also what an organ uses to look back.

The day's statistics, computed from the archive when asked (places, activity minutes, steps, health numbers) for a date (default yesterday). steps is null when the day has no step readings; counts are the readings archived for the day (all 0 = nothing recorded).
The newest reading of each kind (location, activity, battery, ...) and how old each is. No phone call is made; it is what the archive holds.
A calendar event is about to start or changed, from the hand. Archived only; not recorded in the ledger.
The battery level, from the hand. Archived only; not recorded in the ledger.
The screen came on or the app was opened, with how long the owner was away. Archived only; not recorded in the ledger.
A notification arrived on the hand (app, title, text). Archived only; not recorded in the ledger.
A batch of location points from the hand; a batch_id makes a re-delivered batch idempotent. Archived only; not recorded in the ledger.
A batch of activity segments from the hand. Archived only; not recorded in the ledger.
A batch of health readings from the hand. Archived only; not recorded in the ledger.
The owner entered or left a named place. Archived only; an organ that listens decides whether to wake an agent.
A health source stopped bringing new readings for stale_hours (sent once), or came back. last_data_ts is its newest reading; summary is plain Chinese for the owner.

The members you can reach and the words of each that you may call, with the label and whether a call needs the owner's approval (true, or per_call when it is judged per call). Pass a member id to see just that one.
The full contract of a member's words you may call (description, input and result schemas, effect, risk), or of one word.
Search the ledger: messages by text, speaker, lane or thread, newest first. Long bodies are summaries with an attachment reference; read them with service:blobs/read.
Read ledger messages by sequence range, as recorded (secret and sensitive fields masked).
What happened in one turn of an agent: the messages it was given, its tool calls and results (summaries), and what it said.
The detail of one activity entry (a turn's tool calls), paged by offset.
Read a text attachment of a ledger message in pieces. You can read an attachment only when you may read the message that holds it.
Get a binary attachment (an image, a file) of a ledger message as a stream reference. You can get an attachment only when you may read the message that holds it.
Ask the host to wake the device at a time (Unix ms); only the earliest one is kept.
Cancel the host alarm.
Keep the device awake for a while (at most 10 minutes) for a stated reason; released by itself when the time is up.
Release the wake lock before its time is up.
The host's alarm went off (the device woke): the host module passes it on to service:clock.
The network or the power state changed: the host module passes it on to service:agents and service:link (which reconnects the relay).
Hand the local link port and token to the hands on this device (the phone app) so they connect. The token is held in memory and never written down.
Have the host download and install a new kernel package (checked against sha256). Only the owner.
The bodies the hub has bound: its own (body:main) and any computer the owner lent, with whether each is Ash's own or borrowed, and whether it is online.
One body in detail: its body.info (system, resources, work directory, ownership), disk use, and the latest error.
Bind a paired computer as a body: its workspace.* capabilities become available as body:<hand>. An agent asking for this goes through the gate.
Unbind a body: workspace.* goes offline at once; the computer stays as a hand and as a host for local agents. body:main cannot be unbound.

Send the owner a short message; it is acknowledged when recorded and does not wait for a reply or replace ask. kind (default reply): reply, due (a reminder), offer or heads_up (unprompted; an opaque stable dedupe_key keeps a repeat from showing twice). facts are source message or fact ids.
React to one existing message with an emoji; an unknown message id fails. Not for a new explanation: use say for that.

Show the owner a file, image, link, a permission page to switch on, or choices. Showing choices does not itself authorize anything. A permission card only names an Android setting the owner must switch on; calling a capability asks the owner by itself.

A durable question to the owner, who must choose before something continues. Only title is required; a question (the default human_kind) also needs options, while a confirmation without options gets yes and no from the owner's side. detail, source and expires_at are optional: the gate fills them for an approval, the tools fill expires_at from approval_ttl_minutes, and the owner's side ends the question at expires_at (at most seven days). The tools human_ask and human_confirm are this word under two names and take exactly this input. The answer (or the expiry) comes back as the response; an approval does not execute anything by itself. The hub's gate uses this for approval cards.

Open or suggest a page on one of the owner's channels: settings, the activity of a turn, a file (id says which). `client` picks the channel; leave it out for the one the owner is on. Check `opened`: a suggestion may be declined.

Put a question to the agent; what it says in the turn that takes the question is the answer. A quick answer is returned directly, a slow one as a receipt.

Wake the agent for a reason, on a lane (default back), with the facts it needs in context. Its own turn runs; nothing is said to the owner by this. Harmless by itself, so organs (apps) may use it to alert an agent.
